_note: THE DEADLINES ARE ACTED ON BY THE APP. THE CITATIONS ARE READ BY A STRANGER.
Those two halves of a row carry different risk, so they ship at different
levels of confidence and this note is here so nobody has to guess which is
respond_days / extension_days drive delr's own follow-up schedule. Getting
one wrong costs a reminder on the wrong day. 45 + 45 is the near-universal
shape of the US state comprehensive privacy laws and is what is seeded.
citation is printed verbatim into a request that a data broker's compliance
desk reads. A wrong section number is a bluff, checkable in thirty seconds,
and it costs the sender the presumption that they know what they are owed.
So citation is EMPTY on every row that has not been read off the statute by
a human, and core/Compose prints nothing where it is empty -- it names the
act and stops. Filling these in is research, not a session.
Same rule for url: empty until somebody has actually opened it.
A jurisdiction that is not in this file is not a bug. It means the app will
compose a courtesy request against the broker's own posted policy instead
of a demand, which is the honest thing to send from a place with no law.

statutes.name: California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the CPRA
statutes.notes: California also runs the DELETE Act broker registry and the DROP platform; for a registered broker that channel may supersede writing to them directly. See Broker::method == drop.

statutes.name: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act
statutes.notes: Texas also maintains a separate data broker registration regime.

statutes.name: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act
statutes.notes: Oregon also maintains a data broker registry.

statutes.name: Tennessee Information Protection Act
statutes.notes: Effective 2025. Confirm the citation and the enforcement posture before relying on this row -- it is the one Scott will file under.
